integrated_description: Phase 1: Immediately mitigate the highest-risk litter safely and within your own capabilities — avoid handling large, sharp, or hazardous items alone without proper tools or assistance. Phase 2: Assess the situation before any further action — if the camper appears intoxicated, aggressive, or the hazard is large or persistent, escalate to campground staff or rangers rather than engaging directly. Phase 3: Only if the situation feels safe and practical, approach the camper using a low-shame, assistance-framed invitation (e.g., 'Want to grab some of that with me?') rather than corrective language, prioritizing cooperative harm prevention over behavioral correction.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders converged on the same core additions — a safety-conditional gate before direct engagement and an explicit ranger/staff escalation pathway — so these could be fully integrated into a revised three-phase sequence without compromising the original mitigate-then-educate direction. The indirect, assistance-framed phrasing requested by stakeholder_a and the leave-no-trace and feasibility framing from stakeholder_c were incorporated as concrete guidance within their respective phases.
